label: Paper
description: Paper in furniture: Lightweight and design-flexible, but heavily dependent on coating and substrate support.
intro: Paper appears across 3 product families and 5 options, especially on Coffee Tables.
chemistry: Paper in furniture is rarely plain sheet paper. It usually appears as a treated fibre, cord, laminate layer or decorative wrap where cellulose fibres are stabilised by coatings, glue or composite construction.
That gives it surprising usefulness for texture and surface design, but the underlying cellulose still means moisture and abrasion control remain important.
furnitureUse: Paper-based materials work best when they are protected by the full build: wrapped around a stable core, used as a decorative weave or specified as part of a composite surface rather than as a naked structural panel.
Their benefit is often visual lightness and crafted texture. Their limit is that deep water damage and abrasion are much harder to recover from than with solid wood or metal.
care: Moisture and wear note: Paper fibres dislike prolonged wet exposure unless well sealed by resins or coatings.
Care note: Use dry or lightly damp cleaning only and avoid soaking the surface or scrubbing through the finish.
strengths: can create interesting woven or wrapped textures
watchouts: sensitive to moisture if the finish fails
abrasion can reveal the substrate quickly
